is_anopheles.evidence: The paper investigates Anopheles funestus s.s. (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F) and L995S (L1014S) (page 4), and identifies other mutations like L928R, L802S, and T1008M (pages 4, 6, 7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (page 7) provides summary statistics for polymorphism including number of sequences (N) and number of haplotypes (h) for populations in Benin, Uganda, Kenya, and Malawi.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Zambia, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, and Benin (Methods, page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study involving field collection, sequencing, and pyrosequencing of mosquito samples.

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper specifies locations such as Mbinga (Katete District), Chikwawa District, Tihuquine (Chokwe District), Tororo, and Pahou (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection dates are provided for specific sites, e.g., Zambia (2010), Malawi (2009-2010), Mozambique (2009) (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new collections and analyses of Anopheles funestus populations.

supplement.evidence: The necessary data for the assessment is contained within the main text and tables of the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the role of knockdown resistance (kdr) in Anopheles funestus across Africa. The authors genotyped the VGSC gene in field-collected mosquitoes from Zambia, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, and Benin. They found no evidence of the common L1014F/S mutations but identified other rare mutations (L928R, L802S, T1008M) and high polymorphism, concluding that kdr plays a limited role in pyrethroid resistance in this species compared to metabolic resistance.
